OPERATOR ARCHITECTURE STEER (decisive): assume Guice AOP (bindInterceptor/MethodInterceptor) may be used for cross-cutting concerns in the future. own_construction (`new Check(...)`, what the probe used) makes the delegate AOP-INVISIBLE (Guice intercepts only container-constructed instances). So DEFAULT must pivot to external_injection: delegate = unscoped @Inject Guice bean, injected into source, moved deps re-rooted as the DELEGATE's @Inject ctor params and DROPPED from the source ctor (move-injection-point).

INVESTIGATION (client repo): no AOP today (0 bindInterceptor) but heavily Guice-managed (630 @Inject, 32 @Singleton; Admin deps container-constructed via field injection). Existing `new` in views = UI/util only (HorizontalLayout, CSVPrinter), no service-delegate precedent. NON-OBVIOUS HAZARD: the extracted delegate holds MUTABLE view state (a per-view mutable tab-selection field) — a container-managed delegate must be UNSCOPED/view-scoped, NEVER @Singleton, or state leaks across users. own_construction got this right for free via `new`; external_injection must guard it.
